items.text: In bereaved relatives offered follow-up by specialist palliative care services, which strategies (proactive personal contact, timing of the first offer, mode of the offer, risk-based targeting, and outreach adapted for men, interpreter needs or distance) are associated with higher uptake of bereavement support than a written invitation or a single call?
items.population: Bereaved relatives or close friends offered follow-up by inpatient hospice, community or hospital palliative care services
items.intervention: Strategies to increase uptake: proactive personal contact, timing, mode of offer, risk-based targeting, adapted outreach
items.comparator: Written invitation, a single call, or another strategy
items.outcome: Uptake of bereavement support, extracted as accepting an offer and as attending at least one session
items.time: Studies published from 2012 to October 2026; uptake up to 13 months after the death
items.setting: Specialist palliative care services in any country, English-language reports

finer: Feasible in eight weeks with the approved librarian and reviewer time; interesting to the board, volunteers and social worker; novel as an update since March 2022; ethical as a literature review; relevant because it decides the programme redesign.
summary: One PICO review question with two pre-specified uptake definitions.
